Rationale / evidence: B-cell activation, autoantibodies, BAFF axis, T-B costimulation, and pathogenic IgG biology are aligned with antibody intervention. Recent clinical development activity exists for BAFF-R/CD40L/FcRn approaches.
Concerns / unknowns: Dryness/fatigue endpoints are hard; best responder segment is unclear; differentiation versus active B-cell programs may be difficult.
Biomarker / patient selection potential: Anti-SSA/SSB, IgG, RF, complement, ESSDAI/ESSPRI, salivary gland pathology.

Rationale / evidence: Severe fibrotic autoimmune disease with immune, B-cell, vascular, and fibrotic components; extracellular cytokine/chemokine and membrane targets exist.
Concerns / unknowns: Causal target biology is heterogeneous; fibrosis reversal is difficult; safety window for anti-fibrotic immune targets is uncertain.
Biomarker / patient selection potential: Autoantibodies, skin score, FVC/HRCT, inflammatory/fibrotic serum markers, disease duration.

Target candidates: CD19; CD20; BAFF/APRIL; FcRn; plasmablast-associated targets
Rationale / evidence: B-cell/plasmablast biology is strong; IgG4 and organ inflammation provide measurable disease biology; inebilizumab/obexelimab validate antibody tractability.
Concerns / unknowns: CD19 space now has approved/advanced competition; post-CD19 unmet need and new target differentiation are unclear.
Biomarker / patient selection potential: Serum IgG4, plasmablasts, organ imaging, complement, organ-specific activity indices.

Target candidates: CD40L/CD40; BAFF/APRIL; IFNAR1/pDC targets; CD19/CD20; FcRn
Rationale / evidence: Large unmet need with B-cell, IFN, immune complex, and costimulation biology; multiple accessible antibody targets and biomarkers.
Concerns / unknowns: Competitive landscape is crowded; broad SLE heterogeneity dilutes signals; renal outcome trials are long.
Biomarker / patient selection potential: Anti-dsDNA, complement, proteinuria, renal biopsy class, IFN signature, autoantibody profile.

Rationale / evidence: Type I IFN signature, myositis-specific autoantibodies, complement, and B-cell biology suggest antibody-accessible mechanisms.
Concerns / unknowns: Disease heterogeneity; optimal endpoint differs across skin, muscle, and ILD; clinical efficacy for some targets is unproven.
Biomarker / patient selection potential: Myositis-specific antibodies, IFN signature, CK, skin/muscle scores, ILD status.

Target candidates: FcRn; CD20/CD19; IL-4Ralpha; C5/C5a; IgE pathway
Rationale / evidence: Pathogenic autoantibodies are central in pemphigus/BP; antibody titers and skin pathology are measurable; biologic tractability is high.
Concerns / unknowns: FcRn/CD20/IL-4Ralpha competition is increasing; long-term relapse prevention and infection risk need clarification.
Biomarker / patient selection potential: Autoantibody titers, antigen specificity, eosinophils, IgE, complement, lesion counts.

Target candidates: IL-17A/F; IL-36R; OSM/OSMR; IL-1 pathway; TNF
Rationale / evidence: High burden inflammatory skin disease; biologics validate extracellular cytokine targeting; residual nonresponse remains after TNF/IL-17 drugs.
Concerns / unknowns: Biomarker-led patient selection is weak; IL-17/TNF differentiation is weak; effects on tunnels/scarring are uncertain.
Biomarker / patient selection potential: HiSCR, lesion type, inflammatory signatures, microbiome/immune signatures are candidate but not established.

Rationale / evidence: Clear antigen trigger and biomarkers; refractory or symptomatic patients despite gluten-free diet remain unmet; IL-15/lymphocyte pathways are antibody-accessible.
Concerns / unknowns: Most patients managed by diet; anti-cytokine safety in gut immunity; clinical success of antibody approaches remains unclear.
Biomarker / patient selection potential: HLA-DQ2/DQ8, anti-tTG, biopsy, gluten challenge response, refractory disease status.

Target candidates: BAFF/APRIL; CXCL13/CXCR5; integrins/trafficking targets; fibrotic mediators
Rationale / evidence: AIH/PBC/PSC have immune and fibrotic components with limited options in subsets, especially PSC; competition is not overcrowded.
Concerns / unknowns: Antibody necessity is weak; causal extracellular targets are not well established; small molecules/metabolic drugs may be more suitable.
Biomarker / patient selection potential: IgG/IgM, autoantibodies, ALP/bilirubin, fibrosis markers, imaging, histology.

Rationale / evidence: Autoantibody, complement, B-cell, and neutrophil biology make antibody intervention plausible; biomarkers are comparatively clear.

Biomarker / patient selection potential: PR3/MPO-ANCA, renal involvement, complement markers, inflammatory markers, relapse history.
